## 2. Summary of the Judgment

## 3. Analysis

### 3.1 Precedents Cited

#### (a) Braham Dass v. State of Himachal Pradesh, (2009) 7 SCC 353

The High Court extracted the core proposition that for Section 279 (and by extension Section 304A),
the prosecution must establish an “element of rashness or negligence”.
This precedent anchored the legal threshold: criminal liability does not arise merely because an accident occurred; it arises when the
driving is shown to have endangered human life or likely caused injury, reflecting rashness/negligence. [...] ## 4.
